name: Glute bridge
summary: On your back with knees bent, squeeze the buttocks and lift the hips until the body is a straight line from knees to shoulders.
setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. Push through the heels and squeeze the buttocks to lift the hips, pause at the top, lower slowly.
brief: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. Push through the heels and squeeze the buttocks to lift the hips, pause at the top, lower slowly.
why: From the side the shoulder–hip–knee angle opens from bent to straight as the hips rise, which counts each bridge. Ribs flaring and the back arching are hard to see side-on, so they are listed, not judged.
calibrationPose: Lie with your knees bent, about 4-6inches from your hips.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arching the lower back at the top
faults.cue: Squeeze glutes instead of lower back
faults.tip: Height should come from the buttocks, not from pushing the ribs or back up. Stop where the body is straight.

faults.label: Heels rising
faults.tip: Heel pressure puts the work in the glutes; toe pressure sends it to the hamstrings and calves.

faults.label: Feet too far away
faults.tip: If the hamstrings cramp, walk the heels in until the shins are near vertical at the top.

faults.label: Feet too close
faults.tip: Keep feet a little away from hips

guide.stop: Lower back pain, or cramp in the hamstrings.

points.t: Rise until knees, hips and shoulders make one line.
Squeeze the buttocks at the top before lowering.

tempo: Up 2 s, squeeze 2 s, down 3 s.
progression: Single-leg bridge; feet on a step; band above the knees.
regression: Smaller lift; hands on the floor for balance.
contraindications: Lower back pain at the top of the lift, or hamstring cramp.
